preregistration.summary: Solved before opening runs/. A as drafted: ordinary 1,070,000 (§1245 recapture 900k-240k=660k, inventory 10k, covenant 400k); §1374 BIG = (900k+230k)×21% = 237,300 (S election 1/1/2023 → recognition period through 12/31/2027); capital 1,450,000 less §1366(f)(2) loss 237,300 = 1,212,700; total tax 875,740; net 2,224,260. B: 2,850,000-420,000 = 2,430,000 LTCG, tax 486,000, net 2,364,000 (§453 defers the note portion; unsecured note; 10% indemnity cap). Counter: V 650k (register FMV) / VI 50k / VII 2,050k → ordinary 470k, net 2,326,260. Naive 20%×3.1M = 2,480,000 (reference's 2,564,000 applies 20% to price less stock basis). Break-even A price ≈3,147k with counter, ≈3,275k as drafted (any correct computation ±25k accepted). Oracle convention used: strict = within the manifest tolerance for the item (exact for non-numeric); lenient = manifest tolerance + $5 rounding slack. Raw observed values and diffs are recorded in every note so the scorer can re-cut.

fixture_issues: Oracle item 1 tolerance (±25k) is narrower than the effect of the §1366(f)(2) treatment choice (up to ±47,460). The library states only that the §1374 tax is 'treated as a loss sustained by the S corporation'; the reference nets it fully against capital gain (2,224,260). Runs that showed it as a flagged sensitivity (A, C, E: 2,176,800), netted it against ordinary (B: 2,264,601) or allocated it pro rata by BIG source as §1366(f)(2) itself does (D: 2,232,471) all land outside or near the edge of the tolerance. Four of five runs fail this item for that reason alone while agreeing on every component.

Inside asset basis (240k+140k+200k = 580k) exceeds Ray's stock basis (420k) by 160k; after an asset sale a liquidating distribution would produce a further ~160k gain (~32k tax) that the reference ignores. Runs C and E flagged it; graded per key.

The LOI A covenant payment is made to Ray personally while the reference pools it with corporate proceeds into one net; no run was penalised for pooling.

cross_run_observations: All five runs independently agree on the components the key tests: ordinary income 1,070,000 (660k recapture + 400k covenant + 10k inventory), §1374 tax 237,300 with the per-asset caps binding under every allocation, Buyer B net 2,364,000 with §453 deferral on the unsecured note, and a do-not-sign-A-as-drafted recommendation; every run also caught all five traps before the review turn. The only oracle divergence is item 1, and it is entirely a §1366(f)(2) presentation choice: A, C and E keep the full 237,300 as a cost and show the pass-through as a flagged sensitivity (2,176,800); B nets it against ordinary (2,264,601); D splits it pro rata by BIG source (2,232,471, the only one inside the ±25k tolerance). The reference's all-against-capital figure (2,224,260) was computed by nobody as a headline, though A, C, D and E all mention it. Counter allocations differ on Class VI (A: $0; B/C/D/E: $100,000) and inventory (B/C/D: 140k; A/E: 150k); all put equipment at the register's 650k. Run C is the outlier on trust: its arithmetic matches the others but its stale counter/QUESTIONS/comparison files carry invented document facts and fabricated library quotes that the model itself had detected and was repairing when the output cap hit. Run D's review turn was capped before any change; run A's review made real corrections; run B's review added hedging and break-evens.
